entries.literal_english: Obeisance to Śrī Gaṇeśa and Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Oṃ: obeisance to Śrī Rāmacandra, who dwells in the hearts of devotees and whose lotus feet contain the nectar of consciousness relished by the paramahaṃsas. May the garlands of dust from the feet of Kṛṣṇa, supreme bliss, triumph: worn upon the head, they become garlands of glory even for Indra and others. In the eleventh canto, liberation is described in the stated thirty-one chapters, through such narratives as that of the Jāyanteyas, both briefly and in detail. Nārada described it briefly to Vasudeva, while the Lord set it forth at length to Uddhava with supporting arguments. The first chapter introduces the destruction of the Yadu lineage under the designation of the club episode to bring about detachment. Kṛṣṇa's joyful play has been narrated in his activity; in the cessation of that activity, his ascent to the abode of supreme bliss is narrated. In the tenth canto, the pastimes of Śrī Kṛṣṇa were described as a source of joy for people intent on hearing and remembering them. For the removal of Earth's burden, the Lord, accompanied by divine portions descended into the Yadu lineage adorned with his manifestations, imitated conduct suited to his role. Now his ascent to his own abode is narrated: he teaches the devotees the truth of the self, and the divine portions descended to earth for the play resume their respective stations under the guise of the club episode, in favor of Brahmā and the others. At Kurukṣetra Vasudeva, still not detached, asked how karma could be removed through karma; Nārada and the others explained karma-yoga, saying that action is removed through action when the Puruṣa is worshipped with faith using legitimately acquired and pure wealth. Purified through that practice, Vasudeva understood Kṛṣṇa and Rāma to be the Supreme Lord, and Kṛṣṇa taught him the truth of the self in the chapter on bringing back the six sons. Vasudeva said he accepted the coherent teaching about the principles of reality spoken of with regard to them as sons. Excessive sense enjoyment had again concealed that knowledge, so Nārada expounds it anew in the first five chapters. First, the impermanence even of exceedingly elevated sense pleasures is shown through the Yadu family's destruction under the pretext of a Brahmin's curse. Four chapters then set out the supreme reality with its attendant matters through the dialogue of Nimi and the Jāyanteyas; the sixth introduces the Lord's dialogue with Uddhava; twenty-three chapters contain his exposition to Uddhava; and the final two narrate the club episode. Thus begins the explanation, to the extent of my understanding, of the eleventh canto's thirty-one chapters. To establish the context for the club episode, two verses recapitulate the preceding canto, beginning 'Having done.' The form avatārayat should be understood with the augment aṭ; javiṣṭham means very swift, ending in violence; kalim means strife.
entries.editorial_note: Śrīdhara's five introductory stanzas here are his own and not Bhāgavatam 11.1.1–5. The separately attributed Jīva and Viśvanātha sections beginning after this block are excluded. Source citations within Śrīdhara's passage, including 10.84.29, 10.84.37 and 10.85.22, are preserved in the passage above and translated in the literal rendering. This file represents only 11.1.1, not a complete chapter. The exact Śrīdhara source block is retained in the `sanskrit` field after removing Markdown emphasis markers only.
entries.sanskrit: शृई-गणेशाय नमः । श्री-कृष्णाय नमः । ॐ नमः श्री-परम-हंसास्वादित-चरण-कमल-चिन्-मकरन्दाय भक्त-जन-मानस-निवासाय श्री-रामचन्द्राय । विजयन्ते परानन्द-कृष्ण-पाद-रजः-स्रजः । या धृता मूर्ध्नि जायन्ते महेन्द्रादि-महः-स्रजः ॥१॥ उक्तैक-त्रिंशताध्यायैर् मुक्तिर् एकादशे ततः । जायन्तेयेतिहासाद्यैः समास-व्यास-रूपतः ॥२॥ नारदो वसुदेवाय समासेन न्यवर्णयत् । भगवान् उद्धवायाथ विस्तरेणोपपत्तिभिः ॥३॥ तत्र तु प्रथमेऽध्याये यदु-वंशस्य सङ्क्षयः । उपक्षिप्तो विरागाय मौसल-व्यपदेशतः ॥४॥ प्रवृत्तितः परानन्द- कृष्ण-क्रीडानुवर्णिता । तन्-निवृत्त्या परानन्द-पदारोहोऽनुवर्ण्यते ॥५॥ एवं तावद् दशम-स्कन्धे भू-भारावतारणाय निज-विभूति-विभूषित-यदु-वंशस्य यदु-वंशावतारित-सकल-सुरांशस्य भगवतः श्री-कृष्णस्य तद्-उचित-प्रवृत्ति-विडम्बनेन तच्-छ्रवण-स्मरणादि-पराणां परेषाम् आनन्द-कारणं क्रीडा निरूपिता । अथेदानीम् अपरिमित-योगमाया-वैभवस्य भक्तानाम् आत्म-तत्त्वोपदेश-पूर्वकं क्रीडार्थं भू-तलेऽवतारितानां चाधिकारिणां सुरांशानां मौसलापदेशेन तत्-तद्-अधिकार-पद-प्रापण-पूर्वकं च ब्रह्माद्य्-अनुग्रहाय निज-पदारोहो निरूप्यते । तत्र कुरुक्षेत्र-यात्रायाम् अविरक्तस्य वसुदेवस्य, कर्मणा कर्म-निर्हारो यथा स्यान् नस् तद् उच्यतां [भा।पु। १०.८४.२९] इत्य् एवं कर्म-योगं पृष्टवतो नारदादिभिः कर्म-योगो निरूपितः--- कर्मणा कर्म-निर्हार एष साधु निरूपितः । > यच्-छ्रद्धयाप्त-वित्तेन शुक्लेनेज्येत पूरुषः ॥ [१०.८४.३७] > इत्य्-आदिना । तेन च विशुद्ध-सत्त्वस्य श्री-कृष्ण-रामौ परमेश्वरत्वेन ज्ञातवतः षड्-गर्भानयनाध्याये श्री-कृष्णेनात्म-तत्त्वम् उपदिष्टम्--- वचो वः समवेतार्थं तातैतद् उपमन्महे । > यन् नः पुत्रान् समुद्दिश्य तत्त्व-ग्राम उदाहृतः ॥ [भा।पु। > १०.८५.२२] इत्य्-आदिना । तच् च विषय-भोगातिशयेन पुनस् तिरो-हितम् आसीत् तद् एवेदानीं नारद-मुखेन प्रथमं पञ्चाध्याया निरूप्यते । तत्र प्रथमेऽध्याये वैराग्योत्पादनाय यदु-कुलस्य ब्रह्म-शापापदेशेनात्युन्नत-विषय-सुखानाम् अप्य् अनित्यता प्रतिपाद्यते । ततश् चतुर्भिर् निमि-जायन्तेय-संवादेन स-परिकरं परम-तत्त्व-निरूपणम् । ततः षष्ठे भगवद्-उद्धव-संवाद-प्रस्तावः । ततस् त्रयो-विंशत्या उद्धवं प्रति भगवतस् तत्त्व-निरूपणम् । ततो द्वाभ्यां मौसल-क्रीडेत्य् एवम् एक-त्रिंशताध्यायैर् एकादश-स्कन्धस्य प्रवृत्तिः । तस्य च यथामति व्याख्यणम् आरभ्यते । तत्र मौसल-प्रसङ्गार्थं पूर्व-स्कन्धार्थम् अनुवदति श्लोक-द्वयेन---कृत्वेति । अवतारयत् अवतारयद् इत्य् अड्-आगमो द्रष्टव्यः । जविष्ठं वेगवत्तरम् अतिशीघ्रम्, हिंसा-पर्यवसायिनम् इत्य् अर्थः । कलिं कलहम् ॥१॥
